scope: Offline read-only diagnosis of retained device logs and the device vendor APK. This report does not change runtime PASS/NOT_RUN statuses or patch the APK, framework, kernel or modules.

artifact.provenance: Current vendor APK read from the device. No independent claim that its bytes match a separately extracted Sony firmware package.

verified_control_flow: The method iterates a non-null qnpList of QualifiedNetworks records.
A record whose networks field is null or empty enters the no-available-networks branch.
That branch ORs the record APN type into apnTypeMaskNullNw.
When the accumulated mask is nonzero, code at source line 122 explicitly passes a null List to framework updateQualifiedNetworkTypes(mask, null).
The captured crash stack points to this vendor line 122 and the framework List.stream() null dereference. The failure is not a null element inside a non-null List.
vendor_qns.confirmed_conclusion: The installed vendor implementation intentionally creates the null argument on this branch. The observed exception can be explained by this userspace API-contract defect; there is no need to hypothesize that kernel compilation corrupted a Java List.
trigger_not_proven: Which APN mask and physical slot supplied the empty/null networks response in the failed process.
Why this branch was triggered in this boot but not in the other retained captures.
Whether module behavior, timing, SIM provisioning or modem response conditions influenced when the existing defect was reached.

retained_runtime_observation.scope: Same retained exception, not a second independent reproduction; recovery/startup presence does not establish full cellular or VoWiFi functionality.

repair_direction.description: At the vendor caller, represent no qualified networks with a non-null empty List as required by the framework contract. Rebuilding the kernel does not change this APK method.
repair_direction.limits: No APK signing, repackaging, system partition change or runtime hook was attempted; this report does not claim a tested remedy.

established: The recorded init-named fatal processes are not global PID1.
The same-shaped early event also occurs in retained working 40922 evidence and in r3 with modules inactive and enabled.
Global PID1 and system_server continuity were separately observed in the previously published bounded stability evidence.
not_established: The exact parent process, init service name or native abort message.
A shared cause for all early and later non-PID1 events.
That these aborts are harmless, or that a specific kernel or module patch caused them.
init_abort.logging_scope_correction: Retained kernel captures do include some early init messages before one second. The limitation is missing attribution/abort-reason records for these particular processes, not a demonstrated loss of all logs from the first six seconds.
init_abort.mechanism_reference: AOSP distinguishes child abort handling from PID1 fatal handling and can abort a child before exec; this is consistent with the observed process naming but is not device-specific proof of the failing branch.

minimal_discriminating_checks: Review an existing QualifiedNetworksService dump/ring buffer for no-available-networks APN masks without restarting the service; the already-crashed process may have lost its in-memory ring.
For a later normal Wi-Fi/cellular transition, retain before/after crash buffers, QNS process identity and active Internet-network validation; do not infer general Internet from an IMS-only bearer.

If a future already-planned reboot reproduces init aborts, retain any native abort message/tombstone and init start/exit attribution. Do not stop critical services or force another reboot merely to obtain it.
out_of_scope: No claim of complete cellular or VoWiFi validation
